import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy import stats, optimize
pd.set_option("display.width",250)
m5 = pd.read_parquet("mmc5__24h.parquet")
m4a = pd.read_parquet("mmc4__IL33_vs_Vehicle_HUVEC_6_hrs.parquet")
m4b = pd.read_parquet("mmc4__IL33_vs_Vehicle_HUVEC_24_hrs.parquet")
allc = pd.concat([m5, m4a, m4b], ignore_index=True)
# estimate df from t and P for rows with moderate t
sub = allc[(allc.t.abs()>2)&(allc.t.abs()<8)].sample(2000, random_state=1)
def solve_df(t,p):
    f=lambda lg: 2*stats.t.sf(abs(t), np.exp(lg)) - p
    try: return np.exp(optimize.brentq(f, np.log(1), np.log(1e6)))
    except Exception: return np.nan
sub["df_est"]=[solve_df(t,p) for t,p in zip(sub.t, sub["P.Value"])]
print(sub.groupby("Comparison")["df_est"].median().round(2).to_string())
print("overall df quantiles:", sub.df_est.quantile([0.01,0.1,0.5,0.9,0.99]).round(2).to_dict())
# BH check
def bh(p):
    p=np.asarray(p); n=len(p); o=np.argsort(p); r=np.empty(n); 
    q = p[o]*n/np.arange(1,n+1); q=np.minimum.accumulate(q[::-1])[::-1]; r[o]=np.minimum(q,1); return r
res=[]
for c,g in allc.groupby("Comparison"):
    q=bh(g["P.Value"].values); res.append((c, np.max(np.abs(q-g["adj.P.Val"].values)), len(g)))
print(pd.DataFrame(res, columns=["Comparison","max|BH-adj|","n"]).to_string())
EOF

mkdir -p /tmp/outputs/analysis; cat > /tmp/outputs/analysis/sim_voom_pooled_model.R << 'EOF'
# Simulation: does the annex's stated pipeline (single voom/limma group-means fit over
# 114 libraries from 4 heterogeneous cell lines, eBayes(robust=TRUE)) produce
# standard errors (SE = logFC / t) of the size seen in the delivered tables?
# Deliberately adversarial: includes cell-type-restricted genes (zero counts in
# other lines), genes induced from ~0 by IL-33, heavy over-dispersion, and
# outlier libraries.
suppressMessages({library(limma); library(edgeR)})
set.seed(20240611)
arms <- list(HUVEC=c("Veh","NIP","C47","IL33","IL33NIP","IL33C47"),
             HGMEC=c("NIP","C47","IL33","IL33NIP","IL33C47"),
             A549=c("PBS","DMSO","NIP","C47"), MCF7=c("PBS","DMSO","NIP","C47"))
s <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(arms), function(cl) expand.grid(cell=cl, arm=arms[[cl]], time=c("6h","24h"), rep=1:3, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)))
s$group <- factor(paste(s$cell, s$arm, s$time, sep="_"))
stopifnot(nrow(s)==114, nlevels(s$group)==38)
G <- 15000
base <- rnorm(G, 3, 2.5)                         # log2 baseline abundance
type <- sample(c("shared","endo","epi","variable"), G, TRUE, prob=c(.80,.07,.07,.06))
cellshift <- matrix(rnorm(G*4, 0, 1), G, 4, dimnames=list(NULL, names(arms)))
cellshift[type=="endo", c("A549","MCF7")] <- -30   # absent in epithelial lines
cellshift[type=="epi",  c("HUVEC","HGMEC")] <- -30 # absent in endothelial lines
il33 <- rep(0, G); resp <- sample(which(type %in% c("shared","endo")), 600)
il33[resp] <- rnorm(600, 0, 2.5); il33[resp[1:40]] <- runif(40, 6, 11)   # SELE-like induction from ~0
bcv <- ifelse(type=="variable", 0.9, 0.25)
mu <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(s)), function(j){
  l <- base + cellshift[, s$cell[j]]
  if (s$arm[j] %in% c("IL33","IL33NIP")) l <- l + il33
  if (s$arm[j] == "IL33C47") l <- l + 0.1*il33
  2^l })
lib <- runif(114, 15e6, 35e6)
mu <- sweep(mu, 2, colSums(mu), "/"); mu <- sweep(mu, 2, lib, "*")
cnt <- matrix(rnbinom(length(mu), mu=mu, size=1/rep(bcv^2, 114)), G, 114)
# two outlier libraries (e.g. a poor library) to stress the variance model
cnt[, 5]  <- rnbinom(G, mu=mu[,5],  size=1/0.8^2)
cnt[, 70] <- rnbinom(G, mu=mu[,70], size=1/0.8^2)
design <- model.matrix(~0+group, s); colnames(design) <- levels(s$group)
y <- DGEList(cnt); keep <- filterByExpr(y, design); y <- y[keep,, keep.lib.sizes=FALSE]; y <- calcNormFactors(y)
v <- voom(y, design); fit <- lmFit(v, design)
cm <- makeContrasts(
  IL33_vs_Veh_HUVEC_6h = HUVEC_IL33_6h - HUVEC_Veh_6h,
  C47IL33_vs_IL33_HUVEC_6h = HUVEC_IL33C47_6h - HUVEC_IL33_6h,
  C47IL33_vs_IL33NIP_HUVEC_6h = HUVEC_IL33C47_6h - HUVEC_IL33NIP_6h,
  C47_vs_NIP_HUVEC_6h = HUVEC_C47_6h - HUVEC_NIP_6h,
  C47_vs_NIP_HGMEC_24h = HGMEC_C47_24h - HGMEC_NIP_24h,
  C47_vs_PBS_A549_24h = A549_C47_24h - A549_PBS_24h,
  C47_vs_NIP_MCF7_6h = MCF7_C47_6h - MCF7_NIP_6h, levels=design)
f2 <- eBayes(contrasts.fit(fit, cm), robust=TRUE)
se <- abs(f2$coefficients / f2$t)
ratio <- apply(se, 1, max) / apply(se, 1, min)
cat("genes retained:", nrow(se), " voom weight range:", signif(range(v$weights),3), "\n")
cat("SE quantiles (all contrasts):\n"); print(signif(quantile(se, c(.5,.9,.99,.999,1)),3))
cat("max SE in any contrast:", signif(max(se),3), "\n")
cat("within-gene max/min SE ratio quantiles:\n"); print(signif(quantile(ratio, c(.5,.9,.99,.999,1)),3))
cat("IL-33 'SELE-like' induced genes (true log2FC 6-11): min |t| in IL33_vs_Veh:",
    signif(min(abs(f2$t[intersect(rownames(f2), as.character(resp[1:40])), 1])),3), "\n")
out <- data.frame(metric=c("max_SE","SE_q999","ratio_q999","ratio_max","min_abs_t_SELElike","weight_min","weight_max"),
                  value=c(max(se), quantile(se,.999), quantile(ratio,.999), max(ratio),
                          min(abs(f2$t[intersect(rownames(f2), as.character(resp[1:40])), 1])), min(v$weights), max(v$weights)))
write.csv(out, "/tmp/outputs/analysis/sim_voom_pooled_model_summary.csv", row.names=FALSE)
EOF

# 114 libraries from 4 heterogeneous cell lines, eBayes(robust=TRUE)) generate the
# standard errors (SE = |logFC / t|) seen in the delivered mmc4/mmc5 tables?
# The scenario is deliberately adversarial: wide abundance range (many low-count genes),
# genes absent from whole cell lines, SELE-like genes induced from ~zero by IL-33,
# gene-specific over-dispersion up to BCV 1.2, and two grossly outlying libraries.
suppressMessages({library(limma); library(edgeR)})
set.seed(20240611)
arms <- list(HUVEC=c("Veh","NIP","C47","IL33","IL33NIP","IL33C47"),
             HGMEC=c("NIP","C47","IL33","IL33NIP","IL33C47"),
             A549=c("PBS","DMSO","NIP","C47"), MCF7=c("PBS","DMSO","NIP","C47"))
s <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(arms), function(cl) expand.grid(cell=cl, arm=arms[[cl]], time=c("6h","24h"), rep=1:3, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)))
s$group <- factor(paste(s$cell, s$arm, s$time, sep="_"))
stopifnot(nrow(s)==114, nlevels(s$group)==38)
G <- 20000
base <- rnorm(G, 0, 3.5)                                    # wide log2 abundance range
type <- sample(c("shared","endo","epi","variable"), G, TRUE, prob=c(.78,.07,.07,.08))
cellshift <- matrix(rnorm(G*4, 0, 1.5), G, 4, dimnames=list(NULL, names(arms)))
cellshift[type=="endo", c("A549","MCF7")] <- -40            # absent from epithelial lines
cellshift[type=="epi",  c("HUVEC","HGMEC")] <- -40          # absent from endothelial lines
cellshift[type=="endo", c("HUVEC","HGMEC")] <- cellshift[type=="endo", c("HUVEC","HGMEC")] + 6
cellshift[type=="epi",  c("A549","MCF7")]   <- cellshift[type=="epi",  c("A549","MCF7")] + 6
il33 <- rep(0, G); resp <- sample(which(type %in% c("shared","endo")), 800)
il33[resp] <- rnorm(800, 0, 2.5)
sele_like <- sample(which(type=="shared" & base < -2), 40); il33[sele_like] <- runif(40, 7, 12)
bcv <- runif(G, 0.1, 0.4); bcv[type=="variable"] <- runif(sum(type=="variable"), 0.6, 1.2)
mu <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(s)), function(j){
  l <- base + cellshift[, s$cell[j]]
  if (s$arm[j] %in% c("IL33","IL33NIP")) l <- l + il33
  if (s$arm[j] == "IL33C47") l <- l + 0.1*il33
  if (s$cell[j] %in% c("HUVEC","HGMEC")) l[sele_like] <- l[sele_like] - 4  # near-zero baseline in endothelium
  2^l })
lib <- runif(114, 15e6, 35e6)
mu <- sweep(mu, 2, colSums(mu), "/"); mu <- sweep(mu, 2, lib, "*")
cnt <- matrix(rnbinom(length(mu), mu=mu, size=1/rep(bcv^2, 114)), G, 114)
cnt[, 5]  <- rnbinom(G, mu=mu[,5],  size=1/1.0^2)   # outlier library in a HUVEC group
cnt[, 70] <- rnbinom(G, mu=mu[,70], size=1/1.0^2)   # outlier library in an A549 group
design <- model.matrix(~0+group, s); colnames(design) <- levels(s$group)
y <- DGEList(cnt); keep <- filterByExpr(y, design); y <- y[keep,, keep.lib.sizes=FALSE]; y <- calcNormFactors(y)
v <- voom(y, design); fit <- lmFit(v, design)
cm <- makeContrasts(
  IL33_vs_Veh_HUVEC_6h = HUVEC_IL33_6h - HUVEC_Veh_6h,
  C47IL33_vs_IL33_HUVEC_6h = HUVEC_IL33C47_6h - HUVEC_IL33_6h,
  C47IL33_vs_IL33NIP_HUVEC_6h = HUVEC_IL33C47_6h - HUVEC_IL33NIP_6h,
  C47_vs_NIP_HUVEC_6h = HUVEC_C47_6h - HUVEC_NIP_6h,
  C47_vs_NIP_HGMEC_24h = HGMEC_C47_24h - HGMEC_NIP_24h,
  C47_vs_PBS_A549_24h = A549_C47_24h - A549_PBS_24h,
  C47_vs_NIP_MCF7_6h = MCF7_C47_6h - MCF7_NIP_6h, levels=design)
f2 <- eBayes(contrasts.fit(fit, cm), robust=TRUE)
se <- abs(f2$coefficients / f2$t)
ratio <- apply(se, 1, max) / apply(se, 1, min)
sl <- intersect(rownames(f2), as.character(sele_like))
cat("genes retained:", nrow(se), "| residual df:", fit$df.residual[1], "| voom weight range:", signif(range(v$weights),3), "\n")
cat("SE quantiles over all genes x contrasts:\n"); print(signif(quantile(se, c(.5,.9,.99,.999,1)),3))
cat("within-gene max/min SE ratio across contrasts:\n"); print(signif(quantile(ratio, c(.5,.9,.99,.999,1)),3))
cat("SELE-like genes retained:", length(sl), "| min |t| in IL33_vs_Veh:", signif(min(abs(f2$t[sl,1])),3),
    "| median |t|:", signif(median(abs(f2$t[sl,1])),3), "\n")
out <- data.frame(metric=c("genes_retained","max_SE","SE_q999","ratio_q999","ratio_max","SELElike_min_abs_t","SELElike_median_abs_t","voom_weight_min","voom_weight_max"),
                  value=c(nrow(se), max(se), quantile(se,.999), quantile(ratio,.999), max(ratio),
                          min(abs(f2$t[sl,1])), median(abs(f2$t[sl,1])), min(v$weights), max(v$weights)))
write.csv(out, "/tmp/outputs/analysis/sim_voom_pooled_model_summary.csv", row.names=FALSE)
print(out)
EOF

"""
02 - IL-33red response in HUVEC and its neutralisation by Compound_47.
Selection contrast : IL33 vs Vehicle (mmc4)               -> groups {IL33, Veh}
Primary readout    : IL33+C47 vs IL33+NIP228 (isotype)    -> groups {IL33+C47, IL33+NIP}  (no shared group => no shared-noise bias)
Secondary readouts : IL33+C47 vs IL33 (shares the IL33 group with the selection contrast => biased toward apparent reversal)
Derived (logFC algebra on one fitted model, valid for point estimates):
   residual response  IL33+C47 vs Veh   = [IL33 - Veh] + [IL33C47 - IL33]
   isotype effect     IL33+NIP vs IL33  = [IL33C47 - IL33] - [IL33C47 - IL33NIP]
"""
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy import stats
OUT = "/tmp/outputs/analysis/"
tx = pd.read_parquet("/tmp/work/tx_long.parquet")
W = tx.pivot_table(index="ensembl", columns="Comparison", values="logFC")
P = tx.pivot_table(index="ensembl", columns="Comparison", values="adj.P.Val")
ann = tx.drop_duplicates("ensembl").set_index("ensembl")[["symbol", "AveExpr", "flag_any"]]
res_rows = []; gene_tables = []
for tp in ["6hrs", "24hrs"]:
    x = W[f"IL33_vs_Vehicle_HUVEC_{tp}"]; qx = P[f"IL33_vs_Vehicle_HUVEC_{tp}"]
    y_iso = W[f"Compound_47_IL33_vs_IL33_NIP228_HUVEC_{tp}"]; q_iso = P[f"Compound_47_IL33_vs_IL33_NIP228_HUVEC_{tp}"]
    y_il = W[f"Compound_47_IL33_vs_IL33_HUVEC_{tp}"]
    resid = x + y_il
    iso_eff = y_il - y_iso
    for sel_name, sel in {"FDR<0.05 & |logFC|>=1 (SE-flagged genes excluded)": (qx < 0.05) & (x.abs() >= 1) & (~ann.flag_any),

                          "|logFC|>=3 regardless of FDR (incl. SE-flagged)": (x.abs() >= 3)}.items():
        for direction, dmask in {"up": x > 0, "down": x < 0}.items():
            m = sel & dmask

            frac_resid = resid[m] / x[m] * 100         # residual response as % of IL-33 response
            slope = np.polyfit(x[m], y_iso[m], 1)[0] if n > 2 else np.nan
            res_rows.append(dict(timepoint=tp, selection=sel_name, direction=direction, n_genes=n,

                                 pct_genes_opposite_sign_and_FDR05_vs_isotype=np.mean((np.sign(y_iso[m]) == -np.sign(x[m])) & (q_iso[m] < 0.05)) * 100,

                                 median_isotype_effect_logFC=np.median(iso_eff[m]),
                                 median_isotype_effect_pct_of_IL33=np.median(iso_eff[m] / x[m] * 100)))
    g = pd.DataFrame({"IL33_vs_Veh": x, "FDR_IL33_vs_Veh": qx, "C47IL33_vs_NIPIL33": y_iso, "FDR_C47IL33_vs_NIPIL33": q_iso,

res = pd.DataFrame(res_rows)
res.to_csv(OUT + "tables/tx_neutralisation_summary.csv", index=False)
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 30)

"""
09 - Sample-size / power calculations used in the proposal's validation plan.
(a) Approximate per-SD odds ratios for serum markers in the delivered cohort: for a Wald z from a
    logistic model with event fraction p in n patients, standardised log-OR ~ z / sqrt(n p (1-p))
    (Fisher information at beta ~ 0, ignoring covariate-induced variance inflation => conservative).
(b) Power of a replication cohort for a continuous biomarker (simulation, logistic regression).
(c) Donor numbers needed for a re-scored IHC comparison (Mann-Whitney, simulation on an ordinal scale).
"""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from scipy import stats
OUT = "/tmp/outputs/analysis/"
rng = np.random.default_rng(2024)
rep = pd.read_csv(OUT + "tables/serum_unique_proteins_readjusted.csv")
n, ev = 100, 44; p = ev / n
rep["se"] = (np.log(rep.u95) - np.log(rep.l95)) / 3.919928
rep["z"] = np.log(rep.OR) / rep.se
rep["approx_OR_per_SD"] = np.exp(rep.z / np.sqrt(n * p * (1 - p)))
sel = rep[rep.hgnc.isin(["IL1RL1", "HGF", "IL6", "TNFRSF11B", "IL18R1", "CCL20", "CXCL8", "PTX3", "SELE", "VCAM1", "ICAM1", "CSF3"])][["hgnc", "assay", "OR", "l95", "u95", "z", "approx_OR_per_SD"]]
print(sel.round(2).to_string()); sel.to_csv(OUT + "tables/serum_approx_per_SD_OR.csv", index=False)
def power_logit(n, event_rate, or_sd, reps=1500, alpha=0.05):
    b1 = np.log(or_sd); hits = 0
    b0 = np.log(event_rate / (1 - event_rate))
    for _ in range(reps):
        x = rng.standard_normal(n); cov = 0.5 * x + np.sqrt(0.75) * rng.standard_normal(n)  # covariate (e.g. NEWS2) correlated r=0.5 with biomarker
        eta = b0 + b1 * x + 0.5 * cov
        y = rng.random(n) < 1 / (1 + np.exp(-eta))
        try:
            m = sm.Logit(y.astype(float), sm.add_constant(np.column_stack([x, cov]))).fit(disp=0)
            hits += m.pvalues[1] < alpha
        except Exception:
            pass
    return hits / reps
rows = []
for n_ in [100, 150, 200, 300]:
    for er in [0.2, 0.3]:
        for orsd in [1.5, 1.8, 2.0]:
            rows.append(dict(n=n_, event_rate=er, OR_per_SD=orsd, power=power_logit(n_, er, orsd)))
pw = pd.DataFrame(rows); print(pw.pivot_table(index=["n", "event_rate"], columns="OR_per_SD", values="power").round(2).to_string())
pw.to_csv(OUT + "tables/power_replication_cohort.csv", index=False)
# (c) IHC: ordinal 0-5 scores; simulate latent normal shift d (in SD units) -> ordinal via cut points; MW power
def power_mw(n1, n2, d, reps=3000):
    cuts = np.array([-1.5, -0.8, -0.2, 0.4, 1.0])
    h = 0
    for _ in range(reps):
        a = np.digitize(rng.standard_normal(n1) + d, cuts); b = np.digitize(rng.standard_normal(n2), cuts)
        if np.all(a == a[0]) and np.all(b == a[0]): continue
        h += stats.mannwhitneyu(a, b).pvalue < 0.05
    return h / reps
rows = []
for nn in [10, 16, 20, 30, 40]:
    for d in [0.5, 0.8, 1.0]:
        rows.append(dict(donors_per_group=nn, latent_shift_SD=d, power=power_mw(nn, nn, d)))
pm = pd.DataFrame(rows); print(pm.pivot_table(index="donors_per_group", columns="latent_shift_SD", values="power").round(2).to_string())
pm.to_csv(OUT + "tables/power_ihc_donors.csv", index=False)

**Recommendation: NOT YET. Do not start IND-enabling work or clinical dosing of AX-1177 on this package. Approve a 9-month programme of target validation and translational work, with pass/fail criteria fixed in advance, and take the clinical-entry decision at month 9.** --- # AX-1177 (anti-IL-33): proposal to the programme committee **Scope.** I read the whole package in `/tmp/world/filesystem`: the methods annex, `mmc2` (serum proteomics), `mmc3` (post-mortem lung IHC), `mmc4` and `mmc5` (RNA-seq contrasts). I re-analysed it from the delivered tables. Every number below comes from those files. Scripts, tables and figures are in `/tmp/outputs/analysis/`, and `run_all.sh` regenerates everything. Where I use general scientific background that is not in the package, I label it *[background]*. **Naming.** The test article in the package is **Compound_47**. The package never says that Compound_47 *is* AX-1177. I use "Compound_47" for data and "AX-1177" for the programme. Confirming that they are the same molecule is the first gate (G0). --- ## 1. The decision in brief 1. **The package shows one thing well: the antibody works in a dish.** In HUVEC, reduced IL-33 (IL-33red, 30 ng/mL) switches on a large NF-κB inflammatory and adhesion programme: 4,031 genes change at FDR < 0.05 at 6 h. - Compared with the isotype control, Compound_47 blocks **96.1 %** of a 153-gene core IL-33 signature at 6 h (gene-bootstrap 95 % CI 91.9–100.0). - It blocks **73.5 %** at 24 h (67.2–79.3). - On its own, with no IL-33 added, it has no reproducible effect on gene expression in any of the four cell lines. 2. **The package does not show that IL-33 drives viral lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD).** Three observations: - **IL-33 was never measured in patients.** It is absent from all 1,094 delivered serum assays. - **Lung IL-33 staining is not higher in COVID-19.** At donor level it is, if anything, lower in COVID-19 lungs than in controls: endothelium median 4.81 vs 5.50; one-sided p = 0.98 for "higher in COVID+". - **The severity signal in serum is generic inflammation, not IL-33.** Serum proteins that IL-33 induces in endothelium are no more likely than other proteins to track outcome (20.4 % vs 18.6 %; OR 1.12; p = 0.68). 3. **The only IL-33-pathway signal in patients is soluble ST2 (sST2), and it is indirect.** sST2 is one of the two strongest of 1,063 proteins: OR 3.02 per log unit (95 % CI 1.83–5.01), adjusted for age, sex and NEWS2; q ≈ 0.01. But it sits among 186–194 proteins associated at q < 0.05, so it is part of a broad severity signal. It is also SARS-CoV-2-only, from a single centre in the pre-vaccination era. 4. **Everything else needed to go to the clinic is absent:** - potency or IC50 (only one 41:1 antibody-to-IL-33 molar ratio was tested); - any test of oxidised IL-33, although dual binding is the molecule's stated property; - lung cells, and any virus; - in vivo efficacy, PK and safety; - any virus other than SARS-CoV-2. 5. **Data-integrity problems mean even the positive result must be re-derived before anyone relies on it.** The main ones: - The delivered p-values cannot be used for 167 genes. Among them are the classic endothelial-activation genes SELE, VCAM1, CXCL8, CXCL1 and CCL2, which the delivered FDRs call "not significant" despite 4–11 log2 induction. - The serum adjusted p-values were computed over 1,194 tests, but only 1,094 were delivered. - The IHC scores exceed their documented 0–5 scale, and 49 % of COVID+ blocks come from three donors. 6. **Why "not yet" rather than "stop".** The human data are *uninformative* about IL-33 release rather than negative. IHC shows stored IL-33, and serum IL-33 was not measured. The molecule does what it should in vitro. The decisive experiments are cheap and can use samples that already exist: the same 100 sera, and tissue RNA already extracted from 22 of the 31 post-mortem donors. --- ## 2. Evidence scorecard: each link in the therapeutic hypothesis | Link the programme needs | What the package contains | Key numbers | Verdict | |---|---|---|---| | **A. Compound_47 = AX-1177, with adequate potency and species cross-reactivity** | Annex: potency and affinity "held in the programme biologics file… not part of this dataset" | none | **Absent** | | **B. IL-33red activates endothelium** | HUVEC RNA-seq, IL-33red vs vehicle (`mmc4`) | 4,031 / 1,836 genes at FDR < 0.05 (6 h / 24 h). SELE +11.2, CSF2 +10.3, CCL20 +9.2, VCAM1 +8.7, CXCL8 +8.2, ICAM1 +6.0, IL6 +5.8 log2FC at 6 h. Induced genes include 49 % (91/186) of MSigDB Hallmark TNFα→NF-κB genes (OR 43.7) | **Strong in vitro** (single donor, non-lung endothelium) | | **C. Compound_47 neutralises IL-33red** | IL-33+Compound_47 vs IL-33+isotype (NIP228), HUVEC and HGMEC (`mmc5`) | Core signature (n = 153): 96.1 % (91.9–100) at 6 h, 73.5 % (67.2–79.3) at 24 h. ≥ 80 % neutralisation in 81.7 % / 55.6 % of genes. HGMEC: 93.5 % / 78.4 % of core genes reduced | **Strong in vitro, at one 41:1 molar ratio, antibody added at the same time as IL-33** | | **D. No IL-33-independent activity** | Compound_47 vs NIP228 / PBS / DMSO alone, 4 lines × 2 times | 14–73 "hits" per contrast, 53–95 % of them low-abundance. 0–1 hits shared between 6 h and 24 h; genome-wide ρ(6 h, 24 h) between −0.09 and 0.04. No relation to the IL-33 programme (ρ ≤ 0.04, p ≥ 0.45) | **Supported** (transcriptome level only; no Fc-effector cells tested) | | **E. IL-33 is released or active in viral LRTD lungs** | Post-mortem IHC (`mmc3`), 31 donors | COVID+ vs COVID− donors: endothelium Cliff's δ −0.38 (p = 0.052); vascular smooth muscle δ −0.39 (p = 0.068); basal epithelium δ −0.07 (p = 0.76). None higher in COVID+ | **Not supported** (IHC cannot measure release) | | **F. IL-33 pathway activity predicts severity** | Serum Olink panels, 100 patients (`mmc2`) | IL-33 absent. sST2 OR 3.02 (1.83–5.01), q ≈ 0.01. IL-33-induced endothelial products not enriched among outcome-associated proteins (OR 1.12, p = 0.68) | **Weak / indirect** | | **G. Relevant beyond SARS-CoV-2** | none | all human data are SARS-CoV-2, pre-vaccination | **Absent** | | **H. Efficacy, PK, safety and dose in vivo** | none | none | **Absent** | --- ## 3. Problems that change how the package must be read | # | Problem | Evidence | Consequence and fix | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | **Implausible standard errors for 167 genes in the RNA-seq tables** | I derived each SE as \|logFC / t\| (`tables/tx_gene_SE_flags.csv`, `figures/fig3_SE_anomalies.png`).
• Median SE is 0.33; the maximum is **36,723 log2 units**.
• For the same gene, SEs differ up to **225,000-fold** between contrasts. One fit shares each gene's variance across contrasts, so that would need precision weights differing about 10¹⁰-fold.
• A simulation of the annex's pipeline (same 114 libraries and 38 groups, deliberately harsh conditions) never gave an SE above **3.7**, below **0.08**, or a within-gene ratio above **3.6** (`sim_voom_pooled_model.R`).
• The affected genes are cell-type-restricted (CDH5, CD93, VWF, PECAM1; KRT8/19). That fits the annex's single model across four very different cell lines being mis-specified. | The delivered FDRs call **SELE +11.2 (q = 0.50), VCAM1 +8.7 (0.51), CXCL8 +8.2 (0.19), CXCL1 +8.2 (1.00), PTGS2 +4.4 (0.98), CCL2 +4.2 (0.77)** not significant. Any count of "significant genes", or any biomarker choice based on those q-values, is unreliable. I used effect sizes and isotype-controlled contrasts instead. **Fix:** re-fit from the archived counts, one cell type per model. | | 2 | **The wrong comparator inflates neutralisation** | Using the IL-33-alone arm as reference (`Compound_47_IL33_vs_IL33`) gives 82 % reversal of IL-33-repressed genes; the isotype comparator gives 41 %. Annotation comes from offline org.Hs.eg.db 3.18 and MSigDB Hallmark (msigdbr 7.5.1). - **RNA-seq checks.** The limma output is internally consistent: identical AveExpr across all 26 contrasts (one fit); total df 85.13 (76 residual + prior); within-contrast BH reproduced to 5 × 10⁻¹⁵. - **Derived contrasts** (e.g. IL-33+Compound_47 vs vehicle) are logFC arithmetic on that single fit. They are point estimates without SEs. - **Neutralisation estimate.** Percent neutralised = −Σ(Compound_47 vs isotype) / Σ(IL-33 vs vehicle) over the core genes. The two contrasts share no libraries. Selecting genes with large IL-33 effects biases this estimate *downward*, so it is conservative. The CIs come from resampling genes, so they describe the gene set, not replicate-level uncertainty. Replicate-level data were not delivered. - **Serum.** Olink names were mapped to HGNC symbols (`olink_symbol_map.py`; 15 mapped through aliases, listed in the log). Duplicates were collapsed to 1,063 proteins and BH re-run. The "per-SD OR" values are approximations, exp(z/√(n·p·(1−p))), and conservative. - **IHC.** Donor-level Mann–Whitney, HL shifts with bootstrap CIs, Cliff's δ; block-level results are shown only to illustrate pseudo-replication. - **Limits.** - The SE flag (max SE > 5 or min SE < 0.005 log2 units) is a heuristic, backed by the data range (AveExpr −5.1 to 13.5) and the simulation. - The event count (44) is inferred. - I had no raw counts, patient-level serum data or images, so all inference is from summary statistics.

# AX-1177 package re-analysis: file guide

Run `./run_all.sh`, which takes about 5–8 minutes. It regenerates every table and figure cited in `/tmp/outputs/answer.md` from `/tmp/world/filesystem`.

## Scripts, in the order run_all.sh calls them

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `00_export_reference_annotations.R` | Exports offline HGNC alias and MSigDB Hallmark tables to `work/`. |
| `01_load_and_qc_transcriptomics.py` | Reads `mmc4`/`mmc5` directly from xlsx. Checks sheet structure: duplicated sheets, blank padding, labels. Checks limma consistency (df, BH, one fit). Flags genes with implausible implied SE. Writes `work/tx_long.parquet`. |
| `sim_voom_pooled_model.R` | Simulates the annex's stated pipeline (voom/limma, 114 libraries, 38 groups, robust eBayes) under adversarial conditions, to show which SEs it can produce. |
| `02_il33_response_and_neutralisation.py` | HUVEC IL-33red response. Neutralisation against the isotype comparator and against IL-33 alone. Stratification by transcript abundance. Check of whether the isotype effect depends on gene selection. |
| `03_serum_proteomics.py` | `mmc2` structure and panel counts. Inferred event counts. Cross-panel duplicates. Recovery of the 1,194 tests implied by the delivered BH. Re-adjustment on unique proteins. IL-33-axis assays. |
| `04_bridge_serum_to_invitro.py` | Tests whether serum proteins that track outcome are enriched for IL-33-inducible endothelial genes, adjusting for Hallmark NF-κB / inflammatory membership. |
| `05_postmortem_IHC.py` | `mmc3` integrity log. Donor-level aggregation. Group comparisons (Mann–Whitney, Hodges–Lehmann, Cliff's δ, bootstrap CIs). Block vs donor level comparison. Sensitivity analyses. Inventory of tissue RNA. |
| `06_antibody_alone_effects.py` | Compound_47-alone contrasts: hit characterisation, reproducibility, overlap with the IL-33 programme, magnitude compared with control-vs-control comparisons. |
| `07_core_signature_and_pathways.py` | 153-gene core signature. Percent neutralisation with gene-bootstrap CIs (HUVEC, HGMEC). Hallmark over-representation. 24 h replication check. |
| `08_figures.py` | `figures/fig1`–`fig5`. |
| `09_power_and_design.py` | Approximate per-SD ORs. Power for a replication cohort and for IHC donor numbers. |

## Other folders

- `exploratory/` holds the first-pass scratch scripts. They reference `/tmp/work` and are superseded by the numbered pipeline above. Every number cited in the proposal comes from the numbered scripts.
- Key tables:
  - `tables/tx_core_signature_neutralisation.csv`
  - `tables/tx_gene_SE_flags.csv`
  - `tables/tx_canonical_endothelial_genes.csv`
  - `tables/serum_unique_proteins_readjusted.csv`
  - `tables/bridge_enrichment_tests.csv`
  - `tables/ihc_group_comparisons_donor_level.csv`
  - `tables/ihc_data_integrity_log.txt`
- `run_all.log` is the full console output of the last complete run.
